content: Uncertainty guidance consistently says that a numeric uncertainty or confidence statement is meaningful only when its quantity, conditions, method, and probability basis are defined. NIST says a reported uncertainty needs the components and method used to evaluate it; Google PAIR says percentages require enough context for users to understand what they mean; NIST AI RMF calls for documented benchmarks, uncertainty, limitations, human oversight, and recourse. Therefore a provider quality result such as pose or image readiness must remain distinct from real-world measurement accuracy. SukatAI should show observable quality, limitations, provenance, and review state, and keep confidence null or non-numeric unless an independently evaluated reference dataset and protocol support the claim. Sources: https://www.nist.gov/pml/nist-technical-note-1297/nist-tn-1297-7-reporting-uncertainty ; https://pair.withgoogle.com/guidebook-v2/chapter/explainability-trust/ ; https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/
